newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea seen set to slide, US arb helps Med,W.Africa.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea seen set to slide, US arb helps Med,W.Africa.

text.p: The North Sea crude market looked ripe for a fall on Wednesday, while transatlantic trade was helping to prop up differentials for Urals and West African grades, traders said.
Two Brent cargoes, one which turned wet and was kept by a U.S. major, were seen on offer at around Feb Brent +25 cents, after Brent traded at a high of Feb +20 cents on Tuesday.

But traders noted that with next week's CFDs valuing Brent at just Feb +10 cents, sellers were likely to settle for lower. "They're not going to sell at those levels, the market certainly isn't any stronger," said a trader for a European major.
Dealers said there were no real signs of buying from the U.S. which was needed to buoy the North sea market.
Values for Ekofisk eased as a cargo loading Jan 23 traded in the morning at Dated Brent +22, three cents down on Tuesday's trade, while a Jan 28-30 loader later fetched just Dated +18.
Nevertheless a Jan 28-30 Statfjord traded at a firmer Dated Brent +45 cents and another Statfjord was moved on a p+c basis. A Gullfaks loading Jan 22-24 traded at Dated Brent +30.
Brent intermonth spreads slipped lower with Jan/Feb traded at +25 cents and Feb/Mar at +50 and +51 cents.

Feb Brent paper retraced losses and was trading nine cents higher at $24.68 at 1835 GMT in line with the IPE screen. Values dropped to the low $24.20s earlier on the back of bearish weekly stocks data from the United States.

On the Mediterranean sour crude market, Urals was assessed steady to firmer. One trader said that a cargo had traded at a higher level than the Dated Brent -$1.10 deal on Monday, but no further details were given.
Dealers said that an open arbitrage to the United States for sour crudes was expected to lift prices for Urals further, with two traders seen working cargoes transatlantic.
